column1: # Which Juice Shop challenge an agent's lead or evidence names (tools/juiceshop_score.py, D-060).
# One row per indicator: the challenge key, its name in Juice Shop 20.2.0 (checked against the
# catalogue, so a renamed or removed challenge fails loudly), a confidence, a kind, a Python regular
# expression (case-insensitive, matched within one sentence) and why the indicator points at that
# challenge. Columns are separated by one tab. A challenge may have several rows. Every challenge this
# lab can reach (tools/juiceshop/reachable.tsv) has at least one row.
#   firm       the text names the specific issue: its file, path, parameter, value or behaviour,
#              something only this challenge is about (e.g. /ftp/acquisitions.md, /support/logs, an
#              allowlisted URL inside another host's URL). Counted.
#   uncertain  the text names a class of issue that fits this challenge and others, or only a step
#              towards it (e.g. "SQL injection" with no route, the KeePass file without its password).
#              Listed for review, never counted unless a reviewer confirms it.
#   issue      the default: a match counts as the confidence says, subject to the sentence rules below.
#   obtained   a file the challenge is to get past a protection (the /ftp .md/.pdf filter): counted
#              only in a clause that shows it was obtained (a 2xx answer to a request for it, its
#              contents returned, retrieved, downloaded, the bypass), not one that only lists it with
#              other files or says it was refused (403, blocked).
#   group:NAME the indicator names one issue several challenges share (SQL injection in the search,
#              SQL injection in the sign-in): it counts once, for the group's first challenge in this
#              table; for the others it is listed as uncertain. Their own rows (data extracted, a
# Sentence rules, for every row (tools/juiceshop_score.py, tested with the agents' real sentences):
#   absent       a clause that says the issue itself is absent ("no stack trace was shown", "no
#                server-side reflected XSS was observed", "There is no /metrics endpoint") makes the
#                entry's match uncertain. A negation of a protection is not that: "metrics with no
#                authentication", "without the current password", "No Content-Security-Policy" name
#                the issue and stay firm; so does a normative "should not be web-accessible".
#   speculative  a sentence that only supposes the issue ("would", "could", "might", "may",
#                "possible", "should a sink be reachable", "if ... exists", "left open", "requires a
#                browser", "cannot be confirmed") never makes a firm match.
# Challenges without a row cannot be identified from text by this table; they still count when solved.
# Matching runs over the run's leads (title, detail, URL) and evidence (summary, URI) only.
